sentences.text: Leptonectes was an ichthyosaur that lived from the Late Triassic to the Early Jurassic, specifically from the Rhaetian to the Toarcian stages between 205.7 and 182.9 million years ago.
This animal was a medium-sized ichthyosaur, reaching about 4 meters in length, with a skull occupying less than 1 meter of that total size.
The type species, Leptonectes tenuirostris, reached a length of 4 meters.
The largest known species, Leptonectes solei, grew to approximately 5 to 6 meters long.
Another species, Leptonectes moorei, likely reached a length of 3 meters.
Fossils of Leptonectes have been found in Belgium, Germany, Spain, and the United Kingdom.
The genus Leptonectes was previously known by the synonym Leptopterygius, which was named by Huene in 1929.
It is currently debated whether Leptonectes is a monophyletic taxon or a paraphyletic group of basal ichthyosaurs not included in Eurhinosauria, as it lacks a defining synapomorphy.
